source.title: Dissecting Chronos: Sparse Autoencoders Reveal Causal Feature Hierarchies in Time Series Foundation Models

record.tranche_reason: The study uses TopK SAEs and feature ablations to analyze a time-series foundation model, but does not test superposition, feature-overlap geometry, capacity pressure, or whether SAE features are complete or canonical units.
record.gate_note: The study reports SAE-feature ablations and a feature taxonomy. The ablations test causal effects on forecasting, not the superposition geometry or the feature-unit properties specified by the claim versions. The taxonomy assigns concept labels but does not measure feature directions or overlap; cited findings are not recorded as results.
record.test_reason: The study trains TopK SAEs on Chronos-T5-Large, a time-series transformer rather than an LLM, and uses them as a tool. It reports single-feature and progressive ablation effects on forecast CRPS, plus a heuristic correlation-based concept taxonomy. It reports no reconstruction or sparsity quality, no overlap or geometry of feature directions, no capacity analysis, and no completeness, stability or canonicality test of SAE features. No row measures what any version names, so no version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is correct. The authors conclude that SAE features are causally meaningful handles in Chronos-T5-Large and that causal importance peaks in the mid-encoder. They also conclude that the semantically richest final encoder is less causally critical, with progressive ablation there improving or leaving CRPS flat on ETT.
record.recipe_differences: The study applies TopK SAEs and feature ablations to a time-series foundation model; it does not reproduce the original toy-network superposition method or measure its geometric transitions.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary by encoder layer. The final encoder result also differs between the 64-feature and extended 200-feature configurations.

fits_no_version.finding: Every one of 392 single-feature SAE ablations raised CRPS. Impact is heavy-tailed in encoder blocks 5 and 11 and near-uniform in block 23.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In a time-series foundation model, SAE features are causally used in forecasting, with importance varying by depth.

fits_no_version.finding: Progressive ablation of 64 features sharply worsens CRPS in blocks 5 and 11 but improves it in block 23 (3.62 to 2.73). It stays flat in the extended 200-feature run.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The forecasting effect of cumulative SAE-feature ablation depends on encoder layer and configuration.

fits_no_version.finding: A correlation-based taxonomy labels 4.9% of features at block 5, 25.8% at block 11 and 59.8% at block 23, with level-shift features dominating block 11. No rows record this.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE features in time-series transformers align with temporal concepts in a depth-dependent hierarchy.

record.peer_reviewed: ICLR 2026 Workshop on Time Series in the Age of Large Models (TSALM)
record.problems: The study analyzes only Chronos-T5-Large and uses ETT for causal experiments. The authors describe the 256-window, 4-sample ablation configuration as statistically limited; the taxonomy is heuristic, and 82.8% of features remain unlabeled overall.
record.rows_left_out: No additional causal-ablation outcomes reported in the text were omitted. Taxonomy counts from Table 2 were not entered as rows because they classify temporal concepts rather than measure the claim's feature geometry or SAE-unit properties.

untested.parts: No toy models, no feature-overlap geometry, no sparsity-dependent transition.
No test of capacity competition or of dedicated versus shared dimensions by feature importance.
Polysemantic neurons and their causes are not examined.

The system is a time-series foundation model, not an LLM. Feature spread across neurons is not measured, and SAE reconstruction or sparsity quality is not reported. The heuristic taxonomy labels only 17.2% of features.
Completeness, stability across seeds or sizes, and canonicality of SAE features are not assessed. Positive ablation deltas show causal use only.
One-dimensional versus multi-dimensional features are not compared.

record.verdict_notes: The rows' 'none' links and cannot_determine states are appropriate; no row edits are needed. Ablations act on SAE codes and are decoded back, so effects reflect the SAE reconstruction, whose error is not reported. The authors' wording that the information 'cannot be recovered from the remaining features' goes beyond the evidence. The 54.0%/23.3%/4.8% feature-utilization figures (Section 3.3) are not rows but bear on no version.

versions.untested_parts: Toy-model superposition, overlap geometry, sparsity-dependent transitions, and regular geometry.
Capacity competition, dedicated dimensions for important features, and sharing by less important features.
Alternative causes of polysemantic neurons and whether polysemanticity indicates superposition.
The claim concerns LLM representations and feature spread across neurons or directions; the study analyzes a time-series foundation model and does not measure feature spread across neurons.
Completeness, stability, and canonicality of SAE features are not assessed; causal ablation effects alone do not test these properties.
The study does not compare one-dimensional feature directions with multidimensional features.

rows.subject: Chronos-T5-Large
rows.operation_detail: Zeroed one SAE sparse-code feature, decoded the modified activations, and patched them into the forward pass; reported the summary across 64 features.
rows.note: The paper states that all tested features had strictly positive ∆CRPS. This is a causal-importance result, not a test of superposition or feature geometry.
